2_Introduction: The champion device showed a PCE of 25.6185%, with JSC of 26.603 mA/cm², FF of 81.3014%, and VOC of 1.1845 V. The Cs0.05MA0.05FA0.9PbI3.0 (1.65 mol/L) perovskite precursor solution was prepared. The perovskite solutions were spin-coated onto the substrate at 1000 rpm for 5 s and then 5500 rpm for 30 s. According to the antisolvent method, 150 µL of antisolvent was dropped on the film 15 s before the end of the program. Then, the as-prepared perovskite films were transferred onto a hotplate and annealed at 110 °C for 15 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The triple-cation Cs0.05MA0.05FA0.9PbI3.0 composition, utilizing a 1.65 mol/L precursor, optimizes the tolerance factor and A-site entropy, suppressing undesirable phase segregation and minimizing intrinsic lattice strain to reduce the propensity for halide vacancy formation and ion migration. The two-step spin-coating protocol, comprising a 1000 rpm spread step followed by a 5500 rpm thinning step, establishes controlled fluid dynamics for uniform precursor distribution, while the precisely timed antisolvent drip 15 seconds before the end of the program rapidly induces supersaturation, generating a high density of nucleation sites that, upon subsequent thermal annealing at 110°C, coalesce into a dense, pinhole-free polycrystalline film with enlarged grains and reduced grain boundary area. This optimized crystallization pathway, driven by the synergistic interplay of cation mixing, solution concentration, spin kinetics, and antisolvent quenching, effectively suppresses the formation of deep-level traps, particularly PbI2 antisite defects and under-coordinated Pb2+ at grain boundaries, thereby minimizing non-radiative recombination losses and enhancing charge carrier extraction, which collectively yielded a champion device with a VOC of 1.1845 V, a JSC of 26.603 mA/cm², an FF of 81.3014%, and a PCE of 25.6185%.
